title: El Faro: hurricane routing, BRM/SMS, flooding, propulsion loss, downflooding, and survival-craft limits
summary: El Faro is encoded as a marine safety-management and vessel-state case: the NTSB report ties the sinking to Hurricane Joaquin avoidance/weather use, BRM and SMS oversight, flooding/downflooding, loss of propulsion under list/lube-oil pressure, damage-control planning, and survival-craft suitability.

status_history.note: Added as rev0028 marine casualty / watertight-state lane record.

place.location: near Crooked Island, Bahamas / Hurricane Joaquin

claims.claim: The NTSB report states El Faro foundered and sank about 40 nautical miles northeast of the Bahamas while on a route in the direct path of Hurricane Joaquin, and all 33 crew members perished.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause paragraph attributes the sinking to the captain’s insufficient action to avoid the hurricane, failure to use the most current weather information, late crew mustering, and ineffective bridge-resource management, with TOTE oversight and SMS weaknesses as contributors.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB report lists contributing vessel-state and survivability factors including cargo-hold flooding through an open scuttle or damaged piping, propulsion loss from low lube-oil pressure under sustained list, downflooding through unsecured ventilation closures, lack of an approved damage-control plan, and lack of appropriate survival craft.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.system: cargo vessel / weather routing / BRM / safety management system / propulsion and downflooding under storm/list conditions
sequence_of_events: Vessel sailed into Hurricane Joaquin route context; flooding and list developed; propulsion was lost; downflooding and survival-craft factors shaped loss.
